title: design.submit and design.read are published and reachable by a seat
description:
SPIDR child 1b of task-8a6d6660c31c4e119f962d13e6f1505d, split out by architect-20a6d1eb 2026-09-05 when child 1a's roster measured 11 distinct files against the 10-file hard cap. Cut along the INTERFACE axis: task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a owns the CONTRACT and the versioned AGGREGATE; this row PUBLISHES the two kinds and makes them reachable.

dependsOn task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a - the kinds dispatch into its store.

THESE ARE SEAT KINDS, THE EXCEPTION ON THIS BOARD. Every other kind this epic adds is human-only and MCP-EXCLUDED. `design.submit` is submitted BY AN AGENT and `design.read` is read by seats AND the operator, so both must be REACHABLE over MCP. Copying the approval.decide / escalation.decide pattern here would make the design step unstaffable while looking correct in review - that is the single most likely failure of this row.

THE TWO KINDS TAKE DIFFERENT ROUTES TO BEING SERVED, measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04):
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:87-89` builds the served set as ALL command kinds MINUS `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` (:59), PLUS `MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS` (:27). So `design.submit`, being a COMMAND, is served by simply NOT being added to the exclusion roster - there is no positive action, and the mistake would be adding it there out of habit.
- `design.read` is a QUERY: it must be ADDED to `MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS` (:27, beside product_contract.read, graph.get, events.read, documents.source_read) AND given a handler in the dispatch map at `mcp-dispatch-port.ts:302` (`"product_contract.read": answerProductContractRead` is the shape). A query in the roster with no handler advertises a capability the port cannot serve.

DAEMON ROSTER: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (kind, capability, family, PAYLOAD_KEYS), daemon-command-families.ts (the per-kind flag block :83-94), daemon-command-registry.ts (`entryOf` :205-212). TWO PAYLOAD-KEY TEST TABLES must both gain rows and are invisible to a grep for the kind literal: daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts (~:170-182) and daemon-command-registry.test.ts (~:197-203 plus the flat roster ~:283-300).

THE SHARED CONTRACT AND THE GENERATED CLIENT (packages/contracts runtime-vocabulary + `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`) are needed only when the BROWSER must dispatch these kinds. The operator reads the design through child 3's screen; decide at plan time whether that needs the generated client, and if so include it - never hand-edit it, since it pins GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST checked at client-compat.ts:169.
definitionOfDone: `design.submit` and `design.read` are published across the daemon roster (vocabulary kind/capability/family/PAYLOAD_KEYS, families flag, registry entry) with a BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality test enumerating the SERVED kinds from the dispatch seam; verify by deleting each entry from each side in turn and confirming all four deletions go red.

BOTH ARE SEAT-REACHABLE OVER MCP, asserted behaviourally rather than by roster membership: an AGENT-authenticated dispatch of `design.submit` REACHES the handler, and an agent-authenticated `design.read` returns its answer. This is the opposite of every other kind this epic adds, and the arm exists because copying the human-only pattern would make the design step unstaffable while passing review.
`design.submit` is NOT in `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` and NOT in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS - assert both absences explicitly, since each is a place a well-meaning worker would add it by habit.

`design.read` is in `MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS` (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:27) AND has a handler in the dispatch map (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:302 area). Assert BOTH: a query advertised without a handler promises a capability the port cannot serve, and the allowlist's own parity test compares the roster against the port's table.

Both payload-key TEST tables gain their rows (daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts and daemon-command-registry.test.ts, including its flat kind roster) - these are invisible to a grep for the kind literal in production source and have cost this board a rejected plan before.

If the browser must dispatch either kind, packages/contracts' runtime vocabulary and the REGENERATED client move with it (`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`, quoting the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST). If it need not, say so explicitly in the record rather than leaving it ambiguous for child 3.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, plus `pnpm test` if packages/ was touched.
taskRails: SEAT KINDS, NOT HUMAN GATES. Do not add `design.submit` to MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS or HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. The surrounding pattern invites exactly that mistake and it would silently make the design step unstaffable.
A SERVED QUERY NEEDS BOTH a roster entry and a dispatch handler. One without the other is an advertised capability the port cannot serve.
NO AGGREGATE WORK: the contract and the versioned store are task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a's. No wrapper, no mission, no UI.
NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client; run the generator and quote both digests.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE. NO EDITS. (a) THE CONTRACT HALF IS NO LONGER YOURS. This row was reopened because its 10-file roster omitted two mandatory digest mirrors and was already at the cap — the governor's remedy, requested in #architects at 20:07 and executed on 2026-09-06, was to carve the shared-contract work into a leaf. That leaf is task-64d2757c, which publishes ALL FIVE pending strings (`deployment.migrate_down`, `deployment.rollback`, `design.read`, `design.submit`, `project.set_agent_provider`) in ONE digest rotation, and this row now dependsOn it. DROP FROM YOUR ROSTER: runtime-vocabulary.ts, runtime-contract.test.ts, generated-client.ts, generated-coverage.test.ts and both apps/control-room mirrors. DoD-6 of the text you are reading is now the leaf's, and its answer is YES — the browser does dispatch these kinds, which is why the leaf publishes them. Say that in the record rather than leaving it ambiguous, but do NOT act on it here. Where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY. (b) CONFIRM THE LEAF LANDED: `grep -n 'design.submit\|design.read' packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` must hit BOTH. If not, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ['task-64d2757c06494c1f9016c5e2ffdf19fc'] and stop — `ROWS.kind` is typed `RuntimeCommandKind` and this row cannot TYPECHECK first. (c) EXPECT HEAVY COLLISION AND READ BEFORE EDITING. `moe.claim_next_task` reported TWELVE rows sharing files with this one; daemon-command-vocabulary.ts alone is contended by task-04b3ce7e, task-0a56ecee, task-537320ee, task-54b74b80, task-6cbcf5ff, task-b22462cf, task-c422b106 and task-facff1d1. Run `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` first, read any dirty hunks before touching a file, edit AROUND them, and never revert, stash or regenerate a contended file from a HEAD copy. When a gate reds, check whether the failing arm names YOUR kind before attributing it. (d) MEASURE THE COUNT PINS AS LOCATIONS, NOT VALUES — they moved twice yesterday and eight rows are queued to move them again: `git grep -n 'toHaveLength(\|\.size).toBe(\|registry.size).toBe(' -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts`. Note especially the THREE registry.size pins that sit ~850 lines below their siblings; grep, do not eyeball. This row adds TWO kinds, so every roster count moves by two, not one. (e) BASELINE, standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.

WIRE BOTH KINDS — AS SEAT KINDS, WHICH INVERTS THE PATTERN AROUND THEM. `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` and `daemon-command-families.ts`. Add both kinds to the WiredCommandKind union, a family table entry each (put the table in FAMILY_TABLES — `familyCapabilityOf` returns null for an unclaimed kind and `requiredCapabilityOf` THROWS on that null while BUILDING the registry, i.e. at daemon boot rather than in a test), and their PAYLOAD_KEYS entries. PAYLOAD_KEYS KEY ORDER IS THE SERVED ORDER — the registry maps `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` through `entryOf` — so the positions you choose here are the positions you transcribe into REGISTRATION_ORDER in step 4, which is transcribed in INSERTION order and not alphabetically. NOW THE INVERSION, AND IT IS THIS ROW'S WHOLE POINT (rail 1): every other kind this epic adds is human-only, and the surrounding code is dense with that pattern. THESE TWO ARE THE OPPOSITE. `agentCapabilitiesFor` must return a REAL CAPABILITY SET for `design.submit`, NOT null — a seat has to be able to take it, and returning null the way `product_contract.answer_clarification` does would make the design step permanently unstaffable while passing every roster test. Do NOT add either kind to OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS. `daemon-command-families.ts`: add the membership predicates and return their capabilities before the `familyCapabilityOf` fallthrough; do not set a flag that routes either kind into an existing service's dispatch branch, which is how a new kind silently inherits another family's handler.

SERVE THEM, AND SERVE THE QUERY PROPERLY. (1) `daemon-command-registry.ts`: entries for both kinds, delegating to the design store landed by task-5e90317e — `submitDesignRevision` and `readDesignRevision`. Refuse a malformed payload through that slice's own closed code->layer map (`designRefusal` reads the layer from `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS`, so a call site cannot mint a code and layer that disagree); never a layer literal at the throw site, and reuse an already-rostered layer — no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own. This file was already over the 400-line cap at merge-base: keep the addition small and reformat nothing. (2) `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts`: `design.read` joins MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS. THE QUERY HALF NEEDS BOTH HALVES (rail 2) — that roster is the ADVERTISED oracle and `createMcpDispatchPort` exports the SERVED set as `servedMcpQueryKinds()`; the allowlist's own parity test asserts EXACT SET EQUALITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS between them, so a roster entry without a dispatch handler reds immediately and, worse, would advertise a capability the port cannot serve. Add the handler in the dispatch map in the same commit. (3) DO NOT ADD `design.submit` TO MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, and do not add either kind to HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS (rail 1). Both are places a well-meaning worker adds a kind by habit, and either would silently unstaff the design step. Step 4 asserts both absences explicitly.

THE ROSTERS AND THE BEHAVIOURAL ARMS. (1) COUNT PINS, remembering this row adds TWO kinds so every roster count moves by two: `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` — two ROWS entries (agent capability NON-NULL for design.submit, its family, its payloadKeys) and the ROWS/distinct-kind pins; `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` — two matching ROWS entries, both kinds transcribed into REGISTRATION_ORDER at THE SAME INDICES they occupy in PAYLOAD_KEYS, and SIX registry.size/ROWS/REGISTRATION_ORDER pins including the three ~850 lines down; `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts` — both kinds inserted into the hand-written `registryKinds` SET in SORTED order, a third roster whose own comment says a new command writes its own kind there. Take every number from the PRINTED expected-vs-received. (2) DoD-1's BIDIRECTIONAL CHECK ALREADY EXISTS — `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` compares `[...deps.registry.keys()].sort()` (the DISPATCH SEAM, which is what global rail 9 requires) against `ROWS.map(kind).sort()`, both directions spelled out. Adding your ROWS and PAYLOAD_KEYS entries makes it cover both kinds automatically. Do NOT write a parallel arm; the DoD's "delete each entry from each side in turn and confirm all four deletions go red" is a DRILL against that existing assertion, and step 5 runs it. (3) DoD-2, THE ARMS THAT MAKE THIS ROW DIFFERENT, asserted BEHAVIOURALLY and not by roster membership: an AGENT-authenticated dispatch of `design.submit` REACHES THE HANDLER, and an agent-authenticated `design.read` RETURNS ITS ANSWER. A membership assertion would pass while a capability check refused the seat at dispatch. (4) DoD-3, the two absences: `design.submit` is NOT in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and NEITHER kind is in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS — assert both explicitly, because each is exactly where habit would put them. (5) DoD-4: `design.read` is in MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS AND has a dispatch handler — the allowlist parity test covers the set equality; add an arm proving the handler answers.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST — and note that several are contended by other rows, so an empty `git diff` is only YOUR restore proof if the file was clean when you started; if it carried peer hunks, capture a SHA256 before drilling and prove equality after, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Say which proof applies to which path. FOUR DRILLS, and DoD-1 names them: delete the `design.submit` PAYLOAD_KEYS entry only; delete its ROWS entry only; then the same two for `design.read`. Each must red the existing set-equality arm, and the two directions differ — quote the SET DIFFERENCE each time rather than a bare count, because a count tells you something moved and the difference tells you which side. A FIFTH DRILL, and it is the one this row exists for: make `agentCapabilitiesFor` return null for `design.submit` (the human-only shape every neighbouring kind uses) and confirm the DoD-2 agent-reachability arm goes RED. If it stays green, that arm is asserting roster membership rather than behaviour, and the design step could ship permanently unstaffable. (b) GATES — standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row — vitest.config.ts has no `apps/**`, and after the narrowing this row touches NO packages/** file at all, so say that plainly rather than quoting a root count line. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths — with twelve rows sharing these files, check whether a failing arm names YOUR kind before attributing it. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: is `design.submit` reachable by a seat holding only the capability you granted, or did you grant more than it needs; does `design.read` answer over MCP for an agent principal AND refuse a principal with no capability at all; did either kind land in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS or HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS by habit; do the REGISTRATION_ORDER indices match the PAYLOAD_KEYS insertion positions for BOTH kinds; did you touch any packages/** file (the leaf's, not yours); did you overwrite a peer hunk in a contended file. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: that the contract half is task-64d2757c's and this row touched no packages/** file, with `git status --porcelain -- packages/` proving it; that DoD-6's question is answered YES by that leaf; every pin moved by file:line with before/after counts; the FIFTH drill verbatim, since it is the proof the design step is actually staffable; and that the bidirectional set-equality was REUSED rather than duplicated, naming the arm so a QA reading DoD-1 does not hunt for a new test.
